newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, supported by light movement and firm packer demand, dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hog prices were steady to $0.50 higher, with $52.50 to $53.00 trading in the country and $53.50 to $54.50 at plants.

Illinois hog prices were $0.50-$1.00 higher at $52.00- $53.50 in the country and $54.00 at plants. Indiana hog prices were $0.50-$1.00 higher, with $52.50 to $53.00 in the country and $53.50 at plants. Ohio country hog prices were at $50.00- $51.00 and plant prices ranged from $52.00-$53.00.
Cash hog prices were underpinned by increased competition for live supplies from several packers who were closed Monday in observance of Veterans Day.
Higher pork product prices Monday also lent support, with gains led by demand for hams and bellies, market sources said.
Pork product prices Monday were up $0.87 to $0.93 per cwt, with the Number two carcass value up $0.91 at $74.54, according to USDA.
